lesson.title: ਉਪਮਾ ਅਤੇ ਅਲੰਕਾਰ: Simile and Figurative Language
lesson.subject: punjabi

contentBlocks.text: Yesterday you found ਲੈਅ (rhythm) and ਬਿੰਬ (imagery) in poetry. Today, a tool poets use to make an image even more vivid: comparison.

ਉਪਮਾ (simile) directly compares two different things using a comparing word, making an image sharper by connecting it to something familiar. In English this is the 'like/as' comparison; Punjabi poetry uses comparing words the same way. ਉਪਮਾ is one type of a broader category, ਅਲੰਕਾਰ (figurative language/poetic device) — language used for effect beyond its literal meaning. For example: comparing ਪਿਆਰ (love) to something warm and steady, like sunlight on a field, is a simile that makes an abstract feeling concrete and sensory. Write one original simile of your own, comparing an emotion or idea to something concrete from everyday life.
You've now added a second poetic tool, ਉਪਮਾ, to yesterday's rhythm and imagery. Tomorrow we'll look at a specific traditional Punjabi poetic form: ਦੋਹਾ.

objectives: Define ਉਪਮਾ (simile) as a direct comparison between two different things
Write an original simile connecting an abstract idea to a concrete, sensory image
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review yesterday's ਲੈਅ and ਬਿੰਬ.
2. Introduce ਉਪਮਾ and the broader category ਅਲੰਕਾਰ, using the love/sunlight example.
3. Have the child write an original simile connecting an abstract feeling to something concrete.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's topic: the ਦੋਹਾ form.
differentiationTips: Struggling: provide two half-finished similes ('Anger is like ___', 'Hope is like ___') for the child to complete before writing one fully original
Ready for more: ask them to explain why comparing an abstract feeling to something concrete and sensory makes a poem more vivid than stating the feeling directly
Every Gurmukhi word used in this lesson was checked against gurmukhifix's Lexicon before writing
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1. ਉਪਮਾ is a direct comparison between two different things, usually using a comparing word. 2. ਅਲੰਕਾਰ is the broader category of figurative/poetic language ਉਪਮਾ belongs to. 3. A strong simile connects an abstract idea to something concrete and sensory.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses the course's 'Punjabi literary history, poetry, and formal writing' description by building a second real poetic-analysis tool, continuing from Day 1's rhythm/imagery foundation.
